questions.answerText: It has been shown to cause severe necrotizing pneumonia
questions.solution: Correct Option D - It has been shown to cause severe necrotizing pneumonia: Community-acquired methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (CA-MRSA) is known to cause a wide range of infections, including skin and soft tissue infections (such as the case described in the question), abscesses, cellulitis, and severe necrotizing pneumonia. CA-MRSA strains often carry genes that encode for toxins like Panton-Valentine leukocidin (PVL), which contribute to their ability to cause more severe infections, including necrotizing pneumonia. This type of MRSA is also often associated with young, healthy individuals who do not have traditional risk factors for MRSA infections. Incorrect Options: Option A - It is usually resistant to β-lactams and clindamycin: Community-acquired MRSA (CA-MRSA) is defined as MRSA infection that occurs in the absence of health care exposure. CA-MRSA is most often associated with skin and soft-tissue infections in young, otherwise healthy individuals. CA-MRSA and hospital-acquired MRSA differ in their molecular characteristics and antimicrobial susceptibilities. CA-MRSA is usually resistant to β-lactam antibiotics but is usually susceptible to TMP-SMX and clindamycin. Option B - It primarily causes invasive disease in immunocompromised patients (e.g. HIV, transplantation): A multidrug-resistant isolate has been described among men who have sex with men. It has been shown to cause severe pneumonia and skin and soft-tissue infections, even in immunocompetent individuals. CA-MRSA strains are also more likely to produce Panton-Valentine leukocidin (PVL) virulence factor, a cytotoxin that causes leukocyte destruction and tissue necrosis. Option C - Linezolid has poor activity against community-acquired MRSA: Linezolid has activity against CA-MRSA and is FDA-approved for complicated skin and soft tissue infections and hospital-acquired pneumonia. Patients with MRSA infections due to “community-associated" strains have been observed with increasing frequency among patients in hospital settings. CA-MRSA strains may also cause hospital-onset, health care-associated infections because patients who become colonized with CA-MRSA strains in the community may require hospitalization and either transmit these strains to other hospitalized patients or develop an infection while hospitalized (e.g. following surgery or insertion of an invasive device). @Neet_pg_bot

questions.solution: Correct Option A - Sporothrix schenckii Sporothrix schenckii, a dimorphic fungus, is a well-known pathogen present in soil and decaying vegetation. The classic scenario is a gardener who is pricked by the thorn of a bush (usually a rose bush), highlighting the most common mode of entry (traumatic implantation). Upon viewing the organism growing on the plate macroscopically, a white color is apparent at first that develops into a dark brown color with a wrinkled surface. When observing microscopically at 25°C, note the septate hyphae, oval dark microconidia with flower-like arrangements. Sporotrichosis usually involves the cutaneous or subcutaneous tissues and often spreads through adjacent lymphatics, giving rise to the characteristic pink-purple, painless, firm nodular lesions. These nodular lesions may suppress and ulcerate as the infection becomes more advanced. The laboratory identification of Sporothrix is best achieved with tissue biopsy, which is submitted for histopathological examination and culture. Tissue sections require staining with periodic acid-Schiff (PAS), Grocott's methenamine silver (GMS), or Gram stain: look for small narrow-based budding yeast cells (2-5 µm). The only other useful laboratory process is simple culture onto primary isolation media (a serology test is not useful). Cutaneous or lymphatic infection may be treated with itraconazole, however if the infection becomes systemic the patient must be given Amphotericin B and possible surgical debridement. Incorrect Options: Option B - Exophiala species: Exophiala species (depicted below) has a microscopic morphology notable for conidiophores possessing a pigmented spine with annellate arising at lateral and at times right angles with clusters of conidia aggregating at the tip. Option C - Fusarium species: Fusarium species (depicted below) possess slender phialides that give rise to both macroconidia and microconidia. The macroconidia are around 2-4 cells in length and fusiform (hence the name). The microconidia are fusiform to avoid and include 1 or 2 cells. Hence, both macroconidia and microconidia could be present (for this patient with Sporothrix, there would be only microconidia). questions.solution: Correct Option C - Lactic acid: Lactate levels can be monitored to assess hypoperfusion and prognosis. Shock is characterized by inadequate tissue perfusion, leading to increased anaerobic metabolism and lactic acidosis. This increase in lactate may be buffered at first, so ABG may not reflect this change in PH in early shock. Lactate can be used as a marker for tissue hypoperfusion, and a serum level >4 mmol/L strongly correlates with sepsis. Lactate clearance correlates with improved tissue perfusion. As lactate levels increase from 2 to 8 mmol/L, mortality rates also increase from 10-90%. Higher lactate clearance is associated with better prognosis and outcomes. questions.solution: Correct Option D - Oral vancomycin: Antibiotic-associated colitis is a significant superinfection that can occur in hospitalized patients with mild to serious illness. questions.solution: Correct Option A - Benzathine penicillin G at 2.4 million units IM in a single dose: This therapy helps prevent the progression of syphilis in individuals who may have acquired the infection from their partners.
